---
title: "Functions and methods"
---

phplyr's functions are namespaced functions in `Phplyr`. A function marked with a chain method also runs as that method on `phplyr($table)`. Expression methods are called on the vector helpers that `col()` and other functions return.

## Pipes and method chains

| Function | Chain method | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`phplyr()`](chains.qmd#phplyr) |  | Start a method chain on a table. |
| [`pipe()`](chains.qmd#pipe) |  | Apply steps to a value in order. |

## Single-table functions

### Rows

| Function | Chain method | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`filter()`](single-table.qmd#filter) | `->filter()` | Keep rows where every condition is true. |
| [`filter_out()`](single-table.qmd#filter_out) | `->filterOut()` | Drop rows where every condition is true (dplyr 1.2). |
| [`arrange()`](single-table.qmd#arrange) | `->arrange()` | Sort rows by columns or expressions. |
| [`desc()`](single-table.qmd#desc) |  | Descending sort key for `arrange()`, and for rank helpers. |
| [`distinct()`](single-table.qmd#distinct) | `->distinct()` | Unique rows over the given columns (all columns when none are given). |
| [`slice()`](single-table.qmd#slice) | `->slice()` | Rows by 1-based position within each group, like dplyr's `slice()`. |
| [`slice_head()`](single-table.qmd#slice_head) | `->sliceHead()` | First rows of each group. |
| [`slice_tail()`](single-table.qmd#slice_tail) | `->sliceTail()` | Last rows of each group. |
| [`slice_min()`](single-table.qmd#slice_min) | `->sliceMin()` | Rows with the smallest values of `$orderBy` in each group, ordered by it. |
| [`slice_max()`](single-table.qmd#slice_max) | `->sliceMax()` | Rows with the largest values of `$orderBy` in each group, ordered by it. |
| [`slice_sample()`](single-table.qmd#slice_sample) | `->sliceSample()` | Random rows from each group. |
| [`head()`](single-table.qmd#head) | `->head()` | First `$n` rows of the whole table, ignoring groups (like utils::head). |
| [`top_n()`](single-table.qmd#top_n) | `->topN()` | The n rows with the largest wt in each group, ties included, in their original order (superseded by `slice_max()`). |
| [`top_frac()`](single-table.qmd#top_frac) | `->topFrac()` | `top_n()` with a proportion of each group's rows (superseded by `slice_max(prop:)`). |
| [`sample_n()`](single-table.qmd#sample_n) | `->sampleN()` | n random rows from each group (superseded by `slice_sample()`). |
| [`sample_frac()`](single-table.qmd#sample_frac) | `->sampleFrac()` | A proportion of random rows from each group (superseded by `slice_sample(prop:)`). |
| [`add_row()`](single-table.qmd#add_row) | `->addRow()` | Add rows of values. |

### Columns

| Function | Chain method | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`select()`](single-table.qmd#select) | `->select()` | Keep or drop columns. |
| [`rename()`](single-table.qmd#rename) | `->rename()` | Rename columns, new name as the argument name. |
| [`rename_with()`](single-table.qmd#rename_with) | `->renameWith()` | Rename selected columns (all by default) with a function of the old name. |
| [`relocate()`](single-table.qmd#relocate) | `->relocate()` | Move columns. |
| [`mutate()`](single-table.qmd#mutate) | `->mutate()` | Add, replace, or drop (with null) columns, named by argument. |
| [`transmute()`](single-table.qmd#transmute) | `->transmute()` | Like `mutate()`, keeping only the grouping columns and the new columns. |
| [`pull()`](single-table.qmd#pull) | `->pull()` | Extract one column as a PHP list. |

### Summaries

| Function | Chain method | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`summarise()`](single-table.qmd#summarise) | `->summarise()` | One row per group. |
| [`summarize()`](single-table.qmd#summarize) | `->summarize()` | Alias of `summarise()`. |
| [`reframe()`](single-table.qmd#reframe) | `->reframe()` | Like `summarise()`, but each summary may return any number of values (a list). |
| [`count()`](single-table.qmd#count) | `->count()` | Count rows per combination of columns, within any existing groups. |
| [`tally()`](single-table.qmd#tally) | `->tally()` | Count rows in each group (`summarise(n = n())`). |
| [`add_count()`](single-table.qmd#add_count) | `->addCount()` | Like `count()`, but adds the count as a column instead of summarising. |
| [`add_tally()`](single-table.qmd#add_tally) | `->addTally()` | Like `tally()`, but adds the count as a column. |
| [`glimpse()`](single-table.qmd#glimpse) | `->glimpse()` | Print a compact column-by-column summary and return the table unchanged, so it can sit in the middle of a pipeline. |

## Joins, binding, and set operations

### Joins

| Function | Chain method | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`inner_join()`](two-table.qmd#inner_join) | `->innerJoin()` | Rows of x with a match in y, with y's columns. |
| [`left_join()`](two-table.qmd#left_join) | `->leftJoin()` | All rows of x, with y's columns where they match (NA otherwise). |
| [`right_join()`](two-table.qmd#right_join) | `->rightJoin()` | All rows of y, with x's columns where they match. |
| [`full_join()`](two-table.qmd#full_join) | `->fullJoin()` | All rows of both tables. |
| [`semi_join()`](two-table.qmd#semi_join) | `->semiJoin()` | Rows of x that have a match in y (x's columns only). |
| [`anti_join()`](two-table.qmd#anti_join) | `->antiJoin()` | Rows of x that have no match in y. |
| [`cross_join()`](two-table.qmd#cross_join) | `->crossJoin()` | Every combination of rows of x and y. |
| [`nest_join()`](two-table.qmd#nest_join) | `->nestJoin()` | All rows of x, with a list-column (name) holding each row's matching rows of y as a table. |

### join_by()

| Function | Chain method | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`join_by()`](two-table.qmd#join_by) |  | A join specification, as dplyr's `join_by()`. |
| [`closest()`](two-table.qmd#closest) |  | A rolling join. |
| [`within()`](two-table.qmd#within) |  | x's interval [xLower, xUpper] lies within y's [yLower, yUpper]. |
| [`overlaps()`](two-table.qmd#overlaps) |  | x's interval [xLower, xUpper] overlaps y's [yLower, yUpper]. |

### Binding

| Function | Chain method | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`bind_rows()`](two-table.qmd#bind_rows) | `->bindRows()` | Stack tables under the piped one, matching columns by name. |
| [`bind_cols()`](two-table.qmd#bind_cols) | `->bindCols()` | Put tables side by side with the piped one. |

### Set operations and row updates

| Function | Chain method | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`union()`](two-table.qmd#union) | `->union()` | Distinct rows of both tables. |
| [`union_all()`](two-table.qmd#union_all) | `->unionAll()` | All rows of both tables. |
| [`intersect()`](two-table.qmd#intersect) | `->intersect()` | Distinct rows of x that also appear in y. |
| [`setdiff()`](two-table.qmd#setdiff) | `->setdiff()` | Distinct rows of x that don't appear in y. |
| [`symdiff()`](two-table.qmd#symdiff) | `->symdiff()` | Rows in exactly one of the tables. |
| [`setequal()`](two-table.qmd#setequal) | `->setequal()` | True when both tables hold the same distinct rows, in any order. |
| [`rows_insert()`](two-table.qmd#rows_insert) | `->rowsInsert()` | Append rows of y whose keys are new. |
| [`rows_append()`](two-table.qmd#rows_append) | `->rowsAppend()` | Append all rows of y. |
| [`rows_update()`](two-table.qmd#rows_update) | `->rowsUpdate()` | Overwrite x's values with y's for matching keys. |
| [`rows_patch()`](two-table.qmd#rows_patch) | `->rowsPatch()` | Like `rows_update()`, but only fills x's NA values. |
| [`rows_upsert()`](two-table.qmd#rows_upsert) | `->rowsUpsert()` | Update matching keys and insert new ones. |
| [`rows_delete()`](two-table.qmd#rows_delete) | `->rowsDelete()` | Delete rows of x whose keys appear in y. |

## Grouping

### Grouping and ungrouping

| Function | Chain method | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`group_by()`](grouping.qmd#group_by) | `->groupBy()` | Group by columns (names or selectors). |
| [`ungroup()`](grouping.qmd#ungroup) | `->ungroup()` | Remove grouping, or only the named grouping columns. |
| [`with_groups()`](grouping.qmd#with_groups) | `->withGroups()` | Run a table function on the table grouped by `_groups`, then restore the original grouping (superseded in dplyr by `_by`). |

### Group utilities

| Function | Chain method | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`group_vars()`](grouping.qmd#group_vars) | `->groupVars()` | The grouping column names. |
| [`n_groups()`](grouping.qmd#n_groups) | `->nGroups()` | The number of groups (1 for an ungrouped table). |
| [`group_size()`](grouping.qmd#group_size) | `->groupSize()` | Rows in each group, in group order. |
| [`group_indices()`](grouping.qmd#group_indices) | `->groupIndices()` | Each row's 1-based group number. |
| [`group_keys()`](grouping.qmd#group_keys) | `->groupKeys()` | One row per group with the key columns. |
| [`group_rows()`](grouping.qmd#group_rows) | `->groupRows()` | Each group's 1-based row numbers, in group order. |
| [`group_data()`](grouping.qmd#group_data) | `->groupData()` | `group_keys()` with a .rows list-column of each group's 1-based row numbers. |
| [`group_trim()`](grouping.qmd#group_trim) | `->groupTrim()` | Drop unused factor levels from the grouping columns, and with them the empty groups that drop. |
| [`group_split()`](grouping.qmd#group_split) | `->groupSplit()` | Split into a list of ungrouped tables, one per group. |
| [`group_map()`](grouping.qmd#group_map) | `->groupMap()` | Call `fn (Table $group, array $key)` for each group and return the list of results. |
| [`group_modify()`](grouping.qmd#group_modify) | `->groupModify()` | Replace each group with the table `fn (Table $group, array $key)` returns, then put the key columns back in front. |
| [`group_walk()`](grouping.qmd#group_walk) | `->groupWalk()` | Call `fn (Table $group, array $key)` for each group. |
| [`group_nest()`](grouping.qmd#group_nest) | `->groupNest()` | One row per group. |
| [`nest_by()`](grouping.qmd#nest_by) | `->nestBy()` | Nest by the given columns into a rowwise table. |
| [`cur_group_id()`](grouping.qmd#cur_group_id) |  | The current group's 1-based number, inside `mutate()`, `summarise()`, or `reframe()`. |
| [`cur_group_rows()`](grouping.qmd#cur_group_rows) |  | The current group's 1-based row numbers in the table. |
| [`cur_group()`](grouping.qmd#cur_group) |  | The current group's key, as an array of grouping column =&gt; value (dplyr returns a one-row tibble). |

### Row-wise operations

| Function | Chain method | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`rowwise()`](grouping.qmd#rowwise) | `->rowwise()` | Treat each row as its own group, for row-wise summaries. |

| Function | Chain method | Purpose |

| [`n_distinct()`](vectors.qmd#n_distinct) |  | Number of distinct values (or combinations). |
| [`sum()`](vectors.qmd#sum) |  | Sum of x. |
| [`mean()`](vectors.qmd#mean) |  | Arithmetic mean of x. |
| [`median()`](vectors.qmd#median) |  | Median of x. |

| [`var_()`](vectors.qmd#var_) |  | Sample variance (n - 1). |
| [`variance()`](vectors.qmd#variance) |  | Alias of `var_()`. |
| [`quantile()`](vectors.qmd#quantile) |  | Type 7 quantile, R's default. |
| [`iqr()`](vectors.qmd#iqr) |  | Interquartile range (type 7). |
| [`min()`](vectors.qmd#min) |  | Smallest value of x. |
| [`max()`](vectors.qmd#max) |  | Largest value of x. |
| [`first()`](vectors.qmd#first) |  | First value. |
| [`last()`](vectors.qmd#last) |  | Last value. |
| [`nth()`](vectors.qmd#nth) |  | The `$n`-th value, 1-based. |
| [`any()`](vectors.qmd#any) |  | True when any value is true (R's `any()`. |
| [`all()`](vectors.qmd#all) |  | True when all values are true (R's `all()`. |

### Window functions

| Function | Chain method | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`lag()`](vectors.qmd#lag) |  | Previous values. |
| [`lead()`](vectors.qmd#lead) |  | Next values. |
| [`row_number()`](vectors.qmd#row_number) |  | Row numbers. |
| [`min_rank()`](vectors.qmd#min_rank) |  | Ranks with ties sharing the lowest rank (1, 2, 2, 4). |
| [`dense_rank()`](vectors.qmd#dense_rank) |  | Ranks with no gaps after ties (1, 2, 2, 3). |
| [`percent_rank()`](vectors.qmd#percent_rank) |  | min_rank rescaled to [0, 1]. |
| [`cume_dist()`](vectors.qmd#cume_dist) |  | Proportion of values less than or equal to each value. |
| [`ntile()`](vectors.qmd#ntile) |  | Split into `$n` buckets of near-equal size. |
| [`consecutive_id()`](vectors.qmd#consecutive_id) |  | A new id each time the value (or combination) changes. |
| [`cumsum()`](vectors.qmd#cumsum) |  | Running sum. |
| [`cumprod()`](vectors.qmd#cumprod) |  | Running product. |
| [`cummin()`](vectors.qmd#cummin) |  | Running minimum. |
| [`cummax()`](vectors.qmd#cummax) |  | Running maximum. |
| [`cummean()`](vectors.qmd#cummean) |  | Running mean. |
| [`cumall()`](vectors.qmd#cumall) |  | Running `all()`. |
| [`cumany()`](vectors.qmd#cumany) |  | Running `any()`. |
| [`order_by()`](vectors.qmd#order_by) |  | Evaluate a window function with the rows in another order, then put the results back. |

### Conditionals and NA

| Function | Chain method | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`if_else()`](vectors.qmd#if_else) |  | Vectorised if/else. |
| [`case_when()`](vectors.qmd#case_when) |  | The value of the first case whose condition is true, else `$default`. |
| [`case_match()`](vectors.qmd#case_match) |  | Match values like a switch (deprecated in dplyr 1.2 in favor of `recode_values()`). |
| [`replace_when()`](vectors.qmd#replace_when) |  | Like `case_when()`, but rows matching no case keep x's value. |
| [`recode()`](vectors.qmd#recode) |  | Replace values by name (superseded in dplyr by `recode_values()`). |
| [`recode_values()`](vectors.qmd#recode_values) |  | Map values to new values (dplyr 1.2). |
| [`replace_values()`](vectors.qmd#replace_values) |  | Like `recode_values()`, but unmatched values keep their original value. |
| [`coalesce()`](vectors.qmd#coalesce) |  | First non-NA value across the arguments, row by row. |
| [`na_if()`](vectors.qmd#na_if) |  | NA where `$x` equals `$y`. |
| [`between()`](vectors.qmd#between) |  | `$left` &lt;= `$x` &lt;= `$right`. |
| [`near()`](vectors.qmd#near) |  | Equality with tolerance, for floating point. |
| [`when_any()`](vectors.qmd#when_any) |  | Elementwise `any()` across conditions (x \| y \| z). |
| [`when_all()`](vectors.qmd#when_all) |  | Elementwise `all()` across conditions (x & y & z). |

## Selecting columns

### Selectors

| Function | Chain method | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`starts_with()`](tidyselect.qmd#starts_with) |  | Columns whose names start with a prefix (case-insensitive by default). |
| [`ends_with()`](tidyselect.qmd#ends_with) |  | Columns whose names end with a suffix (case-insensitive by default). |
| [`contains()`](tidyselect.qmd#contains) |  | Columns whose names contain a string (case-insensitive by default). |
| [`matches()`](tidyselect.qmd#matches) |  | Columns whose names match a regular expression. |
| [`num_range()`](tidyselect.qmd#num_range) |  | Columns named prefix + number for each number. |
| [`everything()`](tidyselect.qmd#everything) |  | Every column. |
| [`last_col()`](tidyselect.qmd#last_col) |  | The last column, or the one `$offset` before it. |
| [`all_of()`](tidyselect.qmd#all_of) |  | Exactly these columns. |
| [`any_of()`](tidyselect.qmd#any_of) |  | These columns, skipping any that don't exist. |
| [`where()`](tidyselect.qmd#where) |  | Columns for which a predicate holds. |
| [`except()`](tidyselect.qmd#except) |  | Everything except these columns. |
| [`any_selected()`](tidyselect.qmd#any_selected) |  | Columns matched by any of the selections (union). |
| [`all_selected()`](tidyselect.qmd#all_selected) |  | Columns matched by every selection (intersection, like a & b in tidyselect). |
| [`group_cols()`](tidyselect.qmd#group_cols) |  | The grouping columns. |

### across()

| Function | Chain method | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`across()`](tidyselect.qmd#across) |  | Apply functions to columns inside `mutate()` or `summarise()`. |
| [`if_any()`](tidyselect.qmd#if_any) |  | Per-row test that a predicate holds for any of the columns, for `filter()`. |
| [`if_all()`](tidyselect.qmd#if_all) |  | Per-row test that a predicate holds for all of the columns. |
| [`c_across()`](tidyselect.qmd#c_across) |  | The values of the selected columns in the current row, for `rowwise()` tables. |
| [`pick()`](tidyselect.qmd#pick) | `->pick()` | The selected columns of the current group as a table, for use in `summarise()` closures or with `vec()`. |
| [`cur_column()`](tidyselect.qmd#cur_column) |  | The name of the column `across()` is working on, inside one of its functions. |

## Reshaping with tidyr

### Pivoting

| Function | Chain method | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`pivot_longer()`](tidyr.qmd#pivot_longer) | `->pivotLonger()` | Lengthen. |
| [`pivot_wider()`](tidyr.qmd#pivot_wider) | `->pivotWider()` | Widen. |
| [`build_longer_spec()`](tidyr.qmd#build_longer_spec) | `->buildLongerSpec()` | The spec `pivot_longer()` would use, as a table with .name, .value and the namesTo columns. |
| [`pivot_longer_spec()`](tidyr.qmd#pivot_longer_spec) | `->pivotLongerSpec()` | Lengthen with a spec from `build_longer_spec()` (a table or a list of rows). |
| [`build_wider_spec()`](tidyr.qmd#build_wider_spec) | `->buildWiderSpec()` | The spec `pivot_wider()` would use, as a table with .name, .value and the namesFrom columns. |
| [`pivot_wider_spec()`](tidyr.qmd#pivot_wider_spec) | `->pivotWiderSpec()` | Widen with a spec from `build_wider_spec()`. |
| [`gather()`](tidyr.qmd#gather) | `->gather()` | Gather columns into key-value pairs (superseded by `pivot_longer()`). |
| [`spread()`](tidyr.qmd#spread) | `->spread()` | Spread a key-value pair across columns (superseded by `pivot_wider()`). |

### Missing combinations and values

| Function | Chain method | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`complete()`](tidyr.qmd#complete) | `->complete()` | Add missing combinations, filling other columns with NA (or with fill). |
| [`expand()`](tidyr.qmd#expand) | `->expand()` | Every combination of the given columns, per group. |
| [`nesting()`](tidyr.qmd#nesting) |  | Only the combinations that occur in the data, for `complete()` and `expand()`. |
| [`crossing()`](tidyr.qmd#crossing) |  | Every combination of unique values (sorted), as a new table. |
| [`expand_grid()`](tidyr.qmd#expand_grid) |  | Every combination of the values as given, first column varying slowest. |
| [`full_seq()`](tidyr.qmd#full_seq) |  | Every value from the smallest to the largest of x in steps of period. |
| [`fill()`](tidyr.qmd#fill) | `->fill()` | Fill NA with the previous (or next) value, within groups. |
| [`drop_na()`](tidyr.qmd#drop_na) | `->dropNa()` | Drop rows with NA in any of the columns (any column when none are given). |
| [`replace_na()`](tidyr.qmd#replace_na) | `->replaceNa()` | Replace NA per column. |
| [`uncount()`](tidyr.qmd#uncount) | `->uncount()` | Repeat each row by a weight column. |

### Splitting and combining

| Function | Chain method | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`separate_wider_delim()`](tidyr.qmd#separate_wider_delim) | `->separateWiderDelim()` | Split columns on a fixed delimiter into new columns. |
| [`separate_wider_position()`](tidyr.qmd#separate_wider_position) | `->separateWiderPosition()` | Split columns by character widths. |
| [`separate_wider_regex()`](tidyr.qmd#separate_wider_regex) | `->separateWiderRegex()` | Split columns with regular expressions. |
| [`separate_longer_delim()`](tidyr.qmd#separate_longer_delim) | `->separateLongerDelim()` | Split columns on a fixed delimiter into rows. |
| [`separate_longer_position()`](tidyr.qmd#separate_longer_position) | `->separateLongerPosition()` | Split columns into rows of `$width` characters. |
| [`separate()`](tidyr.qmd#separate) | `->separate()` | Split a string column into several (superseded in tidyr, still common). |
| [`separate_rows()`](tidyr.qmd#separate_rows) | `->separateRows()` | Split columns on a regular expression into rows (superseded by `separate_longer_delim()`). |
| [`extract()`](tidyr.qmd#extract) | `->extract()` | Pull regular-expression groups into new columns (superseded by `separate_wider_regex()`). |
| [`unite()`](tidyr.qmd#unite) | `->unite()` | Paste columns together into one. |

### List-columns

| Function | Chain method | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`nest()`](tidyr.qmd#nest) | `->nest()` | Nest columns into a list-column of tables. |
| [`unnest()`](tidyr.qmd#unnest) | `->unnest()` | Unnest list-columns of tables back into rows. |
| [`unnest_longer()`](tidyr.qmd#unnest_longer) | `->unnestLonger()` | Turn each element of list-columns into rows. |
| [`unnest_wider()`](tidyr.qmd#unnest_wider) | `->unnestWider()` | Turn each element of list-columns into columns. |
| [`hoist()`](tidyr.qmd#hoist) | `->hoist()` | Pull components out of a list-column into new columns, before it. |
| [`chop()`](tidyr.qmd#chop) | `->chop()` | Collapse rows into list-columns. |
| [`unchop()`](tidyr.qmd#unchop) | `->unchop()` | Expand list-columns into rows, the reverse of `chop()`. |
| [`pack()`](tidyr.qmd#pack) | `->pack()` | Pack columns into a column of named arrays (tidyr's data frame columns). |
| [`unpack()`](tidyr.qmd#unpack) | `->unpack()` | Spread columns of named arrays into columns, the reverse of `pack()`. |

## Chain methods

`phplyr($table)` starts a chain. Each function above with a chain method runs as that method. These methods belong to the chain itself:

| Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`->get()`](chains.qmd#chain-get) | Return the table. |
| [`->pipe()`](chains.qmd#chain-pipe) | Apply your own functions to the table and continue the chain with the result. |

## Expression methods

Called on a vector helper, such as `col('price')->mul(1.1)`.

| Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`->add()`](databases.qmd#method-add) | x + y. |
| [`->sub()`](databases.qmd#method-sub) | x - y. |
| [`->mul()`](databases.qmd#method-mul) | x \* y. |
| [`->div()`](databases.qmd#method-div) | x / y. |
| [`->mod()`](databases.qmd#method-mod) | x modulo y, R's %%. |
| [`->pow()`](databases.qmd#method-pow) | x to the power y. |
| [`->neg()`](databases.qmd#method-neg) | Negation, -x. |
| [`->eq()`](databases.qmd#method-eq) | x == y. |
| [`->ne()`](databases.qmd#method-ne) | x != y. |
| [`->lt()`](databases.qmd#method-lt) | x &lt; y. |
| [`->le()`](databases.qmd#method-le) | x &lt;= y. |
| [`->gt()`](databases.qmd#method-gt) | x &gt; y. |
| [`->ge()`](databases.qmd#method-ge) | x &gt;= y. |
| [`->between()`](databases.qmd#method-between) | low &lt;= x &lt;= high, inclusive. |
| [`->isIn()`](databases.qmd#method-isin) | True where x is one of the values, R's %in%. |
| [`->isNa()`](databases.qmd#method-isna) | True where x is NA. |
| [`->and()`](databases.qmd#method-and) | Logical and, with R's NA rules. |
| [`->or()`](databases.qmd#method-or) | Logical or, with R's NA rules. |
| [`->not()`](databases.qmd#method-not) | Logical not. |
| [`->desc()`](databases.qmd#method-desc) | Sort in descending order, for `arrange()` and order_by. |
